newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aussie Home Loans cuts fixed rate home loans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aussie Home Loans cuts fixed rate home loans.

text.p: Aussie Home Loans, Australia's largest non-bank mortgage lender, said it has cut its two and three-year fixed rate home loans in expectation that official rates will fall again over the next two months.
It said it has cut its two-year fixed rate loan to 7.80 percent from 7.99 percent, while its three-year rate has been cut to 8.10 percent from 8.40 percent.
Aussie Home loans saw this putting further competitive pressure on the banks.

"Australia is now entrenched in a low inflation and low interest rate cycle, and borrowers can expect to enjoy low, stable rates over the next few years," John Symond, managing director of Aussie Home Loans, said in a statement.

"We expect the Reserve Bank will soon respond to the recent announcement of very low inflation figures," he said. "The changes to our fixed rates anticipate that move, and it's a matter of when, not if, official rates fall."
